items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: Skip that leaves every task terminal on a lifecycle needs_validation run (pipeline-terminal task done, no validation_issues key) sets status complete in the same locked write and returns run_status complete; non-terminal, validation_issues, terminal-task-not-done and failed-recover cases stay untouched; the pipeline-terminal phase mirrors the state machine (deploy, or changelog when deploy_target is none).

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: The status flip is inside recover_phase_task's existing _PhaseTasksLock and lands in its single _write_config call, so the task skip and the run completion persist together or not at all; mark_loop_complete only writes when run_config really says complete and the loop runId matches.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No new input surface: the only new input is the already-normalised skip reason path; no new file paths, subprocesses or secrets.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 13 unit tests walk the real lifecycle (claim/complete) to needs_validation and assert on disk state, both recover CLIs are driven in-process, and one subprocess integration test drives a real gated run to deploy and then single-session-next complete; 7 of the unit tests fail on the unfixed code.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: One linear pass over phase_tasks under a lock that was already held; no extra I/O in the lifecycle write.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: _completion_unblocked sits next to recover_phase_task in phase_task_recovery; the loop-pointer stamp lives in orchestrator_pkg/single_session_recovery (the lifecycle never touches loop state, preserving the SS1 split); every touched file stays under its LOC cap.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: shipwright_run_config.json (producer recover_phase_task, consumers resolve_next_dispatch and the router CLI JSON) and .shipwright/run_loop_state.json (producer mark_loop_complete, consumers load_loop_state/_loop_pointer and handoff_pipeline) are round-tripped by the tests through the real readers; the handoff renderer itself only prints the loop status string and was not separately probed.
